rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī says the surah order is divinely fixed in the Preserved Tablet; the Prophet reviewed what he had gathered with Gabriel, twice in his final year, and al-Tibi agrees.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني في البرهان ترتيب السور هكذا هو عند الله تعالى في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: ابن الحصار
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hassar holds that both surah order and the placement of verses were established by revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحصار [ ترتيب السور ] و وضع الآيات موضعها انما كان بالوحي

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the Qur'an's surahs and verses already followed this order in the Prophet's time, except al-Anfal and Bara'a, as a later hadith indicates.
rows.anchor: وقال البيهقي في المدخل كان القرآن على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرتبا سوره وآياته على هذا الترتيبب إلا الأنفال وبراءة للحديث الآتي فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says many surahs had their order known in the Prophet's lifetime, including the seven long surahs, the hawamim, and al-Mufassal; the rest may have been left to the community.
rows.anchor: ومال ابن عطية إلى أن كثيرا من السور كان قد علم ترتيبها في حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم كالسبع الطوال والحواميم والمفصل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the reports establish more than Ibn Atiyya allowed, leaving only a small remainder on which disagreement might be possible.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر بن الزبير الآثار تشهد بأكثر مما نص عليه ابن عطيه ويبقى منها القليل يمكن أن يجري فيه الخلاف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: As evidence that surah order was known, Ibn al-Zubayr cites the Prophet's instruction to read al-Zahrawayn, identified as al-Baqara and Al Imran; Muslim transmits it.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأوا الزهراوين والبقرة وآل عمران رواه مسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن خالد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr also cites Sa'id ibn Khalid's report that the Prophet recited the seven long surahs in one rak'a and grouped al-Mufassal in another.
rows.anchor: وكحديث سعيد بن خالد أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بالسبع الطوال في ركعة وأنه كان يجمع المفصل في ركعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another cited report says the Prophet recited al-Ikhlas and the two refuge surahs when going to bed; al-Bukhari transmits it.
rows.anchor: وأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان اذا أوى إلى فراشه قرأ قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين أخرجه البخاري

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud called al-Isra, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta Ha, and al-Anbiya among the earliest treasured surahs in his recitation legacy.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن ابن مسعود أنه قال في بني اسرائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء انهن من العتاق الأول وهن من تلادي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas holds that the Prophet arranged the surahs, citing the report that he received the seven long surahs in place of the Torah, the Mathani in place of the Gospel, and al-Mufassal as a special gift.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر النحاس المختار أن تأليف السور على هذا الترتيب من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحديث أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطوال

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar says most surah ordering is fixed by prophetic instruction, citing Aws al-Thaqafi's report about the Prophet's division of the Qur'an into groups of three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, then al-Mufassal.
rows.anchor: وقال الحافظ ابن حجر ترتيب معظم السور توقيفي لحديث أحمد وأبي داود عن أوس الثقفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyuti lists study of verse endings and how each ending suits its verses as one dimension of Qur'anic coherence.
rows.anchor: التاسع بيان فواصل الآى ومناسبتها اللآى التي ختمت بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He includes the relation between each surah's name and its contents among the subjects of coherence.
rows.anchor: العاشر مناسبة أسماء السور لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He proposes explaining why the Qur'an chooses one synonym instead of other possible synonyms.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر بيان وجه اختيار مرادفاته دون سائر المرادفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His method includes famous and anomalous readings, their meanings and knowledge, as one aspect of the Qur'an's inimitability.
rows.anchor: بيان القراءات المختلفة مشهورها وشاذها وماتضمنته من المعاني والعلوم فأن ذلك من جملة وجوه إعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also studies differences among repeated passages, such as additions, omissions, reordered material, or substitution of one word for another.
rows.anchor: بيان وجه تفاوت الآيات المتشابهات في القصص وغيرها بالزيادة والنقص والتقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyuti says he made a concise work specifically on coherence in surah order, largely from his own thinking because few had pursued the subject, and selected only views he approved.
rows.anchor: وأكثره من نتاج فكري وولاد نظري لقلة من تكلم في ذلك أو خاض في هذه المسالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He first titled the work Nata'ij al-Fikr, then renamed it Tanāsuq al-Durar because the latter better fit its subject and added wordplay.
rows.anchor: وقد كنت أولا سميته نتائج الفكر في تناسب السورلكونه من مستنتجات فكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether surah order came by prophetic instruction or the Companions' independent judgment, while they agree verse order was fixed by instruction.
rows.anchor: اختلف العلماء في ترتيب السور هل هو بتوقيف من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو باجتهاد من الصحابة بعد الاجماع على أن ترتيب الآيات توقيفي

rows.speaker: مالك والقاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: The ijtihad position is held by a group including Malik and Qadi Abu Bakr in one of his two opinions, and Ibn Faris states it decisively.
rows.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى الثاني منهم مالك والقاضي أبوبكر في أحد قوليه وجزم به ابن فارس

rows.speaker: جماعة الاجتهاد
rows.claim: Their evidence is that early codices differed: Ali's followed revelation order, Ibn Mas'ud began with al-Baqara, al-Nisa, then Al Imran, and Ubayy's and other codices also differed.
rows.anchor: ومما استدل به لذلك اختلاف مصاحف السلف في ترتيب السور فمنهم من رتبها على النزول وهو مصحف علي

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Ibn Ashta transmits through his chain that Uthman ordered the people to place the long surahs together.
rows.anchor: وفي المصاحف لابن أشتة بسنده عن عثمان أنه أمرهم أن يتابعوا الطول

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: The prophetic-order position is held by another group, including Qadi Abu Bakr in his other opinion and many others.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى الاول منهم القاضي أبو بكر في أحد قوليه وخلائق

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains that the whole Qur'an first descended to the lowest heaven, then came down over twenty-odd years; Gabriel showed the Prophet each surah's and verse's place, so their sequence was prophetic and changing it corrupts the Qur'an's order.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري أنزل الله القرآن كله إلى سماء الدنيا ثم فرقه في بضع وعشرين سنة

none: The shared phrase من الناس is incidental; the poems and their commentary concern rain and mourning, not the verse's petition.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fatik is one who surprises another with harm or killing; a hadith calls faith a restraint on treacherous attack, and al-Duraydi says the term is for someone who acts once resolved.
rows.anchor: والفاتك: الذي يفاجئ غيره بمكروه أو قتل. وفي الحديث: الإيمان قيد الفتك. وقال الدريدي: هو الذي إذا هم بالشيء فعل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternate wording describing enemy footmen appearing and prompting him toward drawing his sword is the more reliable of the two recensions.
rows.anchor: وهي أسلم الروايتين. والعدي: الرجالة الذين يعدون قدام الخيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-adi means the foot soldiers who run ahead of the cavalry; it is a collective form like al-kalib and al-da'in.
rows.anchor: والعدي: الرجالة الذين يعدون قدام الخيل. وهو اسم صيغ للجمع، كالكليب والضئين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first recension, the eye is the heart's lookout, ready to expose and correct what the heart dislikes, especially by watching for the sword to be drawn.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن العين رقيب القلب، والمنتظر لإظهار ما يكرهه وتغييره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqi answers that the lines describe two states: the first is sleep, when the heart stays alert, and the second is wakefulness, when the eye guards the heart.
rows.anchor: قلت: إنه وصف حالتين، بالمتقدم صفة حال النوم، والثاني هو صفة حال اليقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akhlaq means smooth, and al-batik means cutting.
rows.anchor: والأخلق: الأملس. والبانك: القاطع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ila salla, ila can mean with, or it can mark the endpoint: the eye keeps watch until he draws the sword, after which action belongs to the heart.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون إلى بمعنى مع، كما تقول هذا إلى ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase min haddi akhlaq is an expansive expression: the sword is drawn from its sheath and thereby becomes unsheathed, like idioms that place clothing into a body part.
rows.anchor: وقوله: من حد أخلق فيه توسع، لأن السيف يستل من الغمد فيصير مسلولا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sword's motion makes death seem to grin at a formidable opponent, personifying death as certain of striking its target; the teeth image depicts its glee.
rows.anchor: إذا هزه في عظم قرن تهللتنواجذ أفواه المنايا الضواحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqi compares another poem's image of death reaching from every lookout and says it describes the sword and its wielder's force.
rows.anchor:
سقاه الردى سيف إذا سل أومضت ...
إليه تنايا الموت من كل مرقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's reference to a bone of a peer signals that he only confronts someone comparable in courage; attributing the grin to molars is figurative, and al-dawāhik are the teeth that show when laughing.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال في عظم قرن إيذانا بأنه لا يتعرض له إلا من يقارنه بأسا وشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of aqūlu is in the first hemistich of the following verse, beginning with بك الوجبة.
rows.anchor: مفعول أقول أول البيت الذي بعده، وهو قوله بك الوسبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet uses the plural mafāriq for the areas around the crown, treating each part by the parting as its own parting.
rows.anchor: وقال في مفارق لأنه جمعه على ما حوله، كما يقال بعير ضخم العثانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khar means fell, with the verbal noun khurur; suhuq describes a tall palm or donkey.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خر سقط، ومصدره الخرور. والسحوق من النخل والحمر: الطويل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fallen man is compared to a trunk, a familiar simile; al-Marzūqi cites the Qur'anic image of hollow palm trunks and notes that this makes his height vivid.
rows.anchor: وتشبيهه إياه بالجذع من قديم التشبيه، وفي القرآن: " كأنهم أعجاز نخل خاوية ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker says he felled a mighty man with his sword, then taunts him that the great death blow settled on him, not on the person he had sought.
rows.anchor: يقول: لما تمكنت من أغلب قنعته بسيفي فسقط، فقلت متشفيا ومستهينا: أناخت الوجبة بك لا بمن كنت تطلبه لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wajba al-uzma means death; the cited Qur'anic phrase describes sacrificial camels falling on their sides.
rows.anchor: أراد بالوجبة العظمى المنية. وفي القرآن: " فإذا جبت جنوبها ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-abid is a contemptuous prayer against the fallen man; malhab can mean humbled or, alternatively, wounded and cut lengthwise.
rows.anchor: وقوله فابعد دعاء عليه على طريق الاستهانة بما حل به. والملحب: المذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second line likens a drawn sword's flash to the gleaming teeth of death, and al-Marzūqi calls this more eloquent than the earlier image.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل قول تأبط شرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This poet makes death's smile the sword's flash as it leaves the sheath, delighted and confident it will strike the victim.
rows.anchor: جعل ضحك الموت تألق السيف إذا جرد من الغمد سرورا به، وذلك جعله إلى المضروب به ثقة بكونه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awmada and wamada both mean to gleam; the variant reading minaya al-mawt in place of thanaya al-mawt is a corruption.
rows.anchor: إذا لمع. ورواه بعضهم: " أومضت إليه منايا الموت "، وهو تصحيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajl al-qatilin uses a part for the whole and repeats the name for emphasis; the first Ajl may be nominative with the second accusative as apposition or clarification.
rows.anchor: قوله عجل القاتلين وإضافة البعض إلى الكل، وكرره توكيدا. ولك أن تضم عجل الأول وتنصب الثاني على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banu Ajl were owed blood revenge by the poet's tribe, Banu Mazin, but killed an uninvolved stranger from Yuhsab who had been staying with them.
rows.anchor: لكنهم أخذوا غريبا كان جاور بني مازن فقتلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet mocks Banu Ajl for claiming revenge when they killed a foreign guest who had neither sought nor helped win the blood debt.
rows.anchor: فقال هذا الشاعر في مخاطبتهم معيرا، وهازئا متهكما: يا عجل القاتلين بوترهم غريبا كان عندنا من بني يحصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's use of zʿamtum may undermine their claim to have taken their right, their supposed revenge, or both; al-Marzūqi says the last reading is most apt.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يضعف الأمرين جميعا، وهو الأشبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objects of zaʿamtum are omitted, as in the Qur'anic question about alleged partners.
rows.anchor: أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn Ulba al-Harithhi's poem laments enemies overwhelming his people while women or helpless dependents were with them, people whom they were duty-bound to defend.
rows.anchor: حين أحلبت ... علينا الولايا والعدو المباسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-talahhuf is grief over something lost after nearly attaining it; the source gives related exclamations and uses of the verb.
rows.anchor: التلهف يكون على الفائت بعد الإشراف عليه، يقولون: وا لهفاه، ووا لهف أماه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahlafa may be a singular vocative or possessive form; the possessive can shift from kasra plus ya to fatHa and alif, with comparable dialectal forms.
rows.anchor: وقوله ألهفى يجوز أن يكون منادى مفردا، ويجوز أن يكون مضافا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in the lament can lengthen the cry and heighten its expression of grief; al-Marzūqi compares the form with other extended vocatives and possessives.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان ألهف يكون الألف قد زيدت لامتداد الصوت به ليكون أدل على التحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahlabāt means helped: although the term first referred specifically to helping with milking, custom generalized it to assistance of any kind.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " أحلبت ": أعانت. وأصله الإعانة في الحلب خاصة، ثم استمرت في الإعانات كلها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-walaya is the plural of waliyya, a saddlecloth; it can allude either to women or to defenseless people, while another recension reads al-mawali, meaning paternal cousins.
rows.anchor: وروي: " الولايا " وهي جمع الولية، وهي البرذعة، وهي تكون كناية عن النساء إن شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqi cites the mother of Ta'abbaṭa Sharran mourning him and the saying that someone is like a discarded saddlecloth as related usages of the image.
rows.anchor: ويشبه هذا قول أم تأبط شرا تؤبنه: " وا ابناه ليس بعلفوف، حشي من صوف، تلفه هوف "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the variant al-mawali is read, the poet singles out cousins because their estrangement hurts more, as being opposed by kin is like being fought with one's own weapon.
rows.anchor: ومن روى الموالي - وهم أبناء العم - فإنما خصهم بالذكر لأن الجفاء منهم أشد تأثيرا في النفس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqi explicitly cites the Qur'anic phrase عدو لي to illustrate the generic singular al-aduww, whose grammatical form follows the word rather than its intended collective meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن: " فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mubāsil is derived from basāla, bravery; al-Marzūqi says the description agrees with the form of the singular word al-aduww rather than its meaning.
rows.anchor: والمباسل، من البسالة. وأجراه على لفظ العدو لا على معناه.

none: The shared conditional phrase لو أن الله is incidental; the poem mourns a son's early death and does not discuss the verse's regret over guidance.
